what: Field values a vision model transcribed that are not text on the page it cited. Recorded before the Candidates that carried them were deleted; they cannot be regenerated, because re-extracting produces different wrong rows.
why: The empirical basis of ADR-0006 and the regression corpus for field-token verification. Every entry here must stay flagged; if a change to the checker stops flagging one, that is a loosening somebody should have to justify.
what_is_not_claimed: These are not all model errors, and this file does not say which are which. Some are the checker's own limit: where the page's text stream glued a correct value to its neighbour (`freeway1148+60`), the checker cannot see the value and flags a row that is right. Separating the two mechanically was attempted and does not work — `Phonosc ope` against a page reading `phonoscope` is the model splitting a word, `1148+60` against `freeway1148+60` is the page gluing one, and both look identical to a substring test. `page_tokens_containing_an_absent_one` is the field to filter on; entries carrying it are the ambiguous ones. No count here should be read as a number of model errors.

page_note: Every token of the page the value was cited to, so a change to the checker is measured against what it will actually see. An earlier version of this file stored only the value's own present tokens, on the argument that the checker asks nothing else. That was true of the checker as written and false of the file's purpose: it stripped out exactly the glued tokens a loosened checker would match on, so the corpus could not detect the loosening it exists to detect.
